answer: Tie each identity to hardware that cannot be copied. To earn beyond a starter cap, an agent's key must live inside a secure enclave and present a remote-attestation quote whose chip ID the ledger has not seen on another account. One chip, one paid identity: a farm of a thousand keys needs a thousand physical chips, a canyon of cost that software cannot cross. Pay rises one terrace at a time while the same chip keeps attesting across epochs, so renting chips briefly does not pay. A key that moves to a new chip restarts at the bottom, like coral rebuilding a reef.
